subject.summary: Milan Cathedral: the white-marble Gothic cathedral with its stepped five-bay façade, the forest of 135 spires on buttresses and piers, walkable roof terraces, and the octagonal tiburio carrying the main spire and the gilded Madonnina at 108.5 m. Plan traced from a published plan; façade proportions measured from a near-frontal photograph.

identity.feature: Stepped five-bay west façade, 61.5 m between the outer aisle walls (about 70 m across the corner buttresses, from the plan) and 56 m to the central crest, each step crowned by an openwork crest
Six façade buttresses with spires: paired at the ends and around the central portal
Five portals and the baroque and neo-Gothic façade windows
The forest of 135 spires on buttresses and piers
Octagonal tiburio with the main spire and the gilded Madonnina at 108.5 m
Five-aisled nave stepping down in height, three-aisled transept with polygonal ends, polygonal apse with three great windows
Walkable marble roof terraces with flying arches and pierced parapets
